title: C++ Application Binary Interface
content:
Cross-industry C++ compiler interoperability

Initiated industry-wide interoperability and standard compliance effort. Still in use today.

Accordingly, it is used as the standard C++ ABI for many major operating systems on all major architectures, and is implemented in many major C++ compilers, including GCC and Clang.

— Itanium C++ ABI

  • Initiated the project with the help of Cary Coutant (who had written the C ABI)
  • Weekly meetings across the industry: HP, Sun, SGI, IBM, Microsoft, GCC maintainers (CodeSourcery, Red Hat) and others; about 20 engineers who dispatched work to their respective compiler teams
  • Related to HP aC++ and the WIESS exception-handling work on Itanium

title: DB48x - Modern RPL Calculator

links.label: DB48x - Reviving the spirit of HP calculators

content:
A modern recreation of Hewlett-Packard Reverse Polish Lisp (RPL)

Free software for physical calculators or phone apps.

  • A modern rebuild of high-end HP-48 and HP-50 calculators, firmware for low-power ARM SoC
  • Very sensitive to power management on low-power ARM
  • Ships as firmware for real hardware calculators including SwissMicros DM32 and DM42 with low-power ARM SoC
  • DM32: ARM Cortex-M33 (STM32U575); DM42: ARM Cortex-M4 (STM32L476)
  • Rich RPL data types and built-in functions with Lisp-level programming power
  • Targets SwissMicros DM42 and DM32 calculator SoCs (DMCP platform)
  • Firmware-style RPL runtime on ARM microcontroller hardware
  • Simulator tested on macOS and Linux
  • Long-term ports envisioned for ARM HP50/HP49/HP48Gii and HP Prime G1
  • Presented at FOSDEM 2023 with an update in 2024

title: HP aC++ Compiler
content:
C++ compiler for Itanium

Cupertino, Hewlett-Packard California Language Lab (CLL), 1998–2000.

  • Led multi-team pre-silicon cross and native bring-up, kernel and user ABI
  • Front-end team lead: exceptions, templates, performance, precompiled headers
  • Led the 16-team native compiler bring-up, the exception-handling project across 8 teams, and worked with HP-UX on speculation
  • Initiated the common C++ ABI effort (Itanium C++ ABI), proposing a shared Itanium C++ ABI with Cary Coutant and meeting engineers from many companies with Daveed Vandevoorde
  • Represented HP at the C++ standards committee for a short period
  • Redesigned the compiler build system to harmonise build configuration across the 16 teams working on the compiler, which all used different makefile conventions — a distant ancestor of Make-It-Quick

Quote: "An exceedingly sharp engineer" — Mark Mitchell

title: HPVM - Enterprise-grade Itanium virtualization
content:
Enterprise-grade virtualization for high-end Itanium servers

  • Started the project; pre-silicon boot on Ski, then A-step silicon bring-up, through production (7-digit quarterly revenue)
  • Firmware-level VMM for Integrity servers
  • Booted 4-way with a team of 3; asked for 15 kernel engineers to productize, got handed “the keys” to the Tru64 kernel team, eventually leading about 60 kernel engineers
  • Program grew to hundreds of engineers
  • Emulated firmware and platform: UEFI (born on Itanium) running inside the VM, ACPI tables, simulated boot loader and guest boot loaders such as GRUB, PCI/PCIe configuration space, MMIO, DMA, a virtual BMC, MCA (Itanium machine-check architecture), NUMA topologies (core / die / package coherence and performance domains), power-management hints critical to performance
  • Features including para-virtualized I/O and on-line guest migration
  • Longest single professional project (~10 years)

Quote: "At HP he was sought after as one of the top strategic visionaries" — Dale Morris

title: XL
content:
Extensible language designed to evolve

  • Renamed from LX after discussions notably with Daveed Vandevoorde; focus shifted from experimental to extensible
  • Re-implemented on Mozart (itself largely reusing LX code)
  • Inherited advanced generics from LX
  • XL2 — re-implementation with a simplified parse tree (8 node types), still used in XLR, Tao3D, and ELFE; meta-programming friendly
  • XL2 was bootstrapped in three stages (first stage in C++)
  • XLR — Extensible Language Runtime; initially an LLVM-backed dynamic back-end for XL2; became a language of its own

Quote: "Advanced and revolutionary stuff" — Raphaël Manfredi

title: XLR8
content:
Super-fast VM for XL

  • XLR8 is a super-fast VM with interpreted and JIT modes
  • Significantly faster than Lua or Python VMs on a sample of micro-benchmarks
  • In JIT mode, it runs within 20% of C/C++ on most tests
  • XLR8 includes its own from-scratch JIT, targeting x86, ARM and RISC-V in 32- and 64-bit modes
  • A full LLVM target generating XLR8 bytecode runs many C and C++ programs
  • Bytecode can be evaluated while bytecode is running, so the runtime itself is extensible
  • XLR8 is intended as the next runtime for XL
